body:
incident-bot: Pager: sev2 - sustained 5xx spike on /v1/generate (hosted, us-west-2). Alert: kv_cache_miss_rate > 30% and continuous_batching_latency_p95 rising. Paging maya (on-call).
maya: seeing it on graphs. 5xxs up ~12% of requests in the last 3 min. top route: model=rw-instruct-3-toolcall, route=tool-runner
liam: getting logs now. a bunch of structured outputs from tool calls — JSON blobs with variable metadata fields. suspicion: tool/function calling is breaking batching/kvcache keys
vikram: I think tool outputs include ephemeral timestamps and session ids, which change prefix tokens and inflate cache misses. also noticed a recent batcher change rolled out ~2h ago (continuous-batching: enable_kv_cache_on_toolcalls=true)
safiya: omg that flag — we enabled it in last sprint to save cost. maybe it's backfiring for tool flows. those outputs are long and variable length, could be forcing small/broken batches
maya: immediate mitigation plan: 1) toggle the flag off for the affected route, 2) shorten batching window to reduce perf cliff, 3) if needed, fallback to model-variant no-kvcache. anyone object?
liam: agree. I'll prepare a hotfix PR and a console toggle. prefer console toggle first for speed.
maya: @deploy-bot can we flip feature flag on route=tool-runner? we need to set continuous-batching.enable_kv_cache_on_toolcalls=false for rw-instruct-3-toolcall
deploy-bot: Received request: toggle feature on route=tool-runner. Confirming current commit id: c3f9a2. Applying toggle...\nDone. change id: toggle-2026-03-15-01-02
vikram: monitoring... kv_cache_miss_rate starting to drop (graph). 5xxs declining but not fully back to baseline
safiya: pushing config patch to reduce batching window from 40ms -> 15ms to avoid big combinatorial batches. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/continuous-batcher/pull/487
liam: applying staging change now, then prod (hotfix). command: 
```
redwoodctl config set /routes/tool-runner/continuous_batching/window_ms 15 --env=prod
```
maya: hold that prod change until toggle has had 5m. want to confirm no downstream regressions.
oncall-sre: note — customers on Dedicated may not honor feature toggle; we should also put an emergency doc for enterprise accounts to advise temporary route pinning.
maya: agreed. patching the console doc now. short advisory in #customer-notify once we have stable numbers.
vikram: with toggle off, cache hit ratio improved from 62% -> 88% on the route. latency p95 dropped ~350ms. still seeing occasional spikes when tool outputs are extremely large.
safiya: quick additional safety: add an upload-size cap to tool runner so we avoid crazy outputs, and normalize tool metadata (remove ephemeral session ids from the prefix). that's a longer-term fix.
liam: executing rollback of the batcher kernel change that was deployed 2h ago (it had a subtle key normalization change). rollback started: deploy-bot executing rollback to c3f9a1
deploy-bot: Rollback in progress... pods draining, new pods up (2/3), migration hooks running. ETA ~60s
maya: calling customers: @support-team please open a CS ticket for any customer reporting 5xxs in last 2 hours. mention: likely transient due to KV cache blowup from toolcalls. template: "We've mitigated an issue causing elevated 5xxs for tool-enabled routes; feature toggle applied; monitoring ongoing."
support: on it, making a consolidated ticket and pinging known affected accounts.
vikram: rollback complete. kernel change reverted. batch metric now stable. continuous-batching.window_ms change still pending.
maya: ok go ahead with window_ms change to 15ms in prod now liam.
liam: applied. command output: \n```
OK: config updated for /routes/tool-runner/continuous_batching/window_ms -> 15
```
maya: monitoring... pv95 improving across hosts. 5xxs at baseline now for most customers. marking incident as mitigated but not resolved. will run postmortem.
safiya: creating a followup issue: normalize-tool-output + do not enable kvcache on toolcalls by default until we have deterministic prefixing. tagging eng-runtime, eng-ml, product.
maya: handoff — oncall shift ends in 30m. @vikram can you take next oncall watch and own the postmortem draft? I'll close the page once we confirm 15m stable.
vikram: taking handoff. I'll own postmortem and customer impact calc. initial impact: ~12% of hosted traffic, zero data loss, customers saw transient 5xxs and increased latency. severity: S2
deploy-bot: Incident incident-1768501234: state -> mitigated by toggle + rollback. ETA to close after 15m stable.
maya: thanks everyone. followups: 1) postmortem (ENG-PRIORITY), 2) change default to not use kv_cache on toolcalls, 3) add unit tests for structured-output normalization, 4) update runbook about toolcall-KV interactions.
vikram: acknowledged. I'll post draft in #postmortems once ready and link customers.
maya: incident clear at 1768503210. Paging closed. :white_check_mark:\n
